# The Bredge | Canonical Knowledge and Service Index

> A source-linked summary of Bredge's public services, published articles and decision resources. It is not a substitute for the original articles.

Publisher: The Bredge
Canonical site: https://thebredge.com/
Contact: hello@thebredge.com

## What The Bredge offers

- Data engineering, analytics and business intelligence: https://thebredge.com/services
- Embedded data team for a continuing data backlog: https://thebredge.com/services/embedded-data-team
- Defined-scope data projects and handover: https://thebredge.com/services/data-projects
- Data Diagnostic to map issues and prioritise next actions: https://thebredge.com/data-diagnostic
- Bredge original analysis of public statistical releases: https://thebredge.com/research

The Bredge helps growing and mid-market organisations reconcile conflicting data, define important measures, automate recurring reporting and improve the reliability of systems feeding business decisions. Work is scoped around the actual source problem.

## Published Insights (canonical URLs and descriptions)

### How to automate reporting for a small business without a data team
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/first-reporting-stack
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: Most small businesses do not need a data platform. They need the five numbers they rebuild every Monday to appear on their own, correct, with one person spending a few hours a month keeping it that way. Here is the smallest setup that does that, and what not to buy.

### Why don't Finance and Sales revenue numbers match?
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/why-dashboards-disagree
Published: 2026-07-14; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data reliability
Summary: The board pack says one number, the CRM says another, and Finance has a spreadsheet with a third. Every figure has an explanation. Here is how to find it before anyone rebuilds a dashboard.

### How to calculate MRR from Stripe, and why yours doesn't match
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/saas-metrics-from-stripe
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data reliability
Summary: MRR summed from invoices, MRR from the Stripe dashboard and MRR in the board deck are three different numbers. Annual plans, prorations, coupons, failed payments and currencies each move them apart. Here is how to define it once and break it into movements a board can read.

### How to connect QuickBooks Online and Xero to Power BI in 2026
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/connect-quickbooks-xero-to-power-bi
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Analytics & BI
Summary: Microsoft has retired its QuickBooks Online connector, there has never been a Microsoft connector for Xero, and Xero now prices API access by connections and data. Here are the routes that still work, what each costs to run and which to choose.

### How to handle GDPR deletion requests in a data warehouse
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/gdpr-deletion-requests-data-warehouse
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: Deleting a customer from the CRM takes a minute. Deleting them from the warehouse, its history tables, Time Travel, backups and every Power BI model built on top is an engineering job. Here is how to find the person, purge or pseudonymise them everywhere, and prove it.

### When to hire a data team, and who to hire first
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/when-to-hire-a-data-team
Published: 2026-07-21; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Running a data function
Summary: More data work does not always mean more headcount. How to tell when you have outgrown one analyst, and whether your first move is a hire, a project, or an embedded team.

### How to calculate ARR for investors: the bridge, cohorts and definitions they ask for
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/investor-ready-arr
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data reliability
Summary: In diligence, buyers rebuild your ARR from contracts, billing and recognised revenue. If yours does not tie, the conversation moves from growth to trust. Here is the evidence pack to build before anyone asks: written definitions, an ARR bridge, a customer-by-month table and cohort retention.

### Why don't Shopify sales, payouts, Xero and GA4 match?
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/shopify-payouts-xero-ga4-revenue
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data reliability
Summary: Shopify shows one sales figure, the bank receives less, Xero shows a third number and GA4 a fourth. Each measures something different. Once you know what each one counts, you can build one revenue figure and a bridge to the others.

### How to prove a data warehouse migration didn't change the numbers
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/warehouse-migration-parity
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data reliability
Summary: Migrations stall at sign-off because nobody can show that the new platform produces the same figures as the old one. Parity is provable: compare row counts by day, key sets, column hashes and measure totals, in that order, and explain every difference.

### How to automate monthly management reporting without making it fragile
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/automate-monthly-reporting
Published: 2026-08-08; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Analytics & BI
Summary: Automating a monthly report the wrong way just moves the fragility somewhere you can no longer see it. What to move upstream, what to leave in Excel, and how to keep it auditable.

### Do you need a data warehouse yet? Six questions to decide
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/before-you-build-a-data-warehouse
Published: 2026-07-28; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: A warehouse solves specific problems. Build it before you have them and you inherit cost and complexity you did not need. Six questions that decide whether it is time.

### Power BI licensing for small businesses: Pro, Premium Per User or Fabric?
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/power-bi-licensing-small-business
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Analytics & BI
Summary: Power BI Pro now costs $14 per user per month and every viewer needs a licence unless the content sits on a large Fabric capacity. For a small business the right answer depends on how many people view reports, how big the model is and how often it refreshes.

### Why doesn't HubSpot closed-won revenue match what Stripe billed?
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/crm-closed-won-vs-stripe
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data reliability
Summary: The CRM says the team closed one number this quarter; Stripe billed another. Both are right about different things. Here is how to link deals to subscriptions, measure the lag between closing and billing, and report a gap the board can read.

### How to model multi-entity consolidation and FX translation in a data warehouse
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/multi-entity-consolidation
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Analytics & BI
Summary: The group pack is assembled from three ledgers, three currencies and a spreadsheet of intercompany balances that never quite nets to zero. A warehouse can carry most of that mechanically, if it is modelled the way finance actually consolidates.

### How to reduce BigQuery and Snowflake costs on billion-row tables
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/incremental-models-at-scale
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: At a few million rows, a full rebuild every night is fine. At a few billion, the same model scans years of history to add one day. The levers that fix it are well documented; most teams pull only one of them.

### Power BI or a data warehouse: which do you need first?
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/power-bi-warehouse-or-both
Published: 2026-08-09; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: "We need better reporting" hides three different problems. Separating the reporting layer, the model and the integration tells you what to buy, and in what order.

### How to match customers across HubSpot, Stripe and Xero
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/one-customer-view
Published: 2026-08-04; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: HubSpot, Stripe and Xero each create their own customer record, with their own ID. Until those records are linked, revenue per customer, churn and pipeline-to-cash reports are guesses. Here is how to link them with rules you can see and test.

### Fabric capacity throttling explained: why Power BI reports stop loading
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/fabric-capacity-throttling
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Analytics & BI
Summary: Executives open a report and it hangs, or fails with a capacity error. On Microsoft Fabric, that is usually throttling: the capacity has borrowed so much future compute that Fabric starts delaying, then rejecting, work. Here is how the stages work, how to find the cause and how to size an F SKU.

### Power BI refresh failed: how to fix the common errors
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/power-bi-refresh-failed
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Analytics & BI
Summary: The dashboard shows yesterday's numbers and the refresh history is red. Most failures come down to five causes: memory, query folding, the gateway, credentials and timeouts. Here is how to tell which one you have and fix it.

### Why is Power BI so slow, and how do you fix it?
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/power-bi-slow
Published: 2026-08-09; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Analytics & BI
Summary: A slow Power BI report is usually a data-model problem wearing a dashboard costume. Where the time actually goes, and the model choices that fix it.

### How to automate repeated Excel data cleaning with Power Query
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/excel-cleaning-automation
Published: 2026-08-09; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Analytics & BI
Summary: If you repeat the same clean-up every month, it is a transformation waiting to be written down once. The Power Query steps that do it, what to fix at source, and what Excel should still do.

### How to reduce Fivetran costs under MAR pricing
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/reduce-fivetran-costs
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: Fivetran bills on monthly active rows, now counted per connection, and since January 2026 deletes count too. The bill is driven by a handful of tables that change constantly. Find them, then decide whether to stop syncing them, sync them differently or move them.

### How to reduce Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks costs at the platform level
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/warehouse-platform-costs
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: Model tuning saves money query by query. The settings around the models decide whether you pay for idle warehouses, unbounded scans and interactive clusters running batch jobs. Here are the platform-level levers on each, from the vendors' own documentation.

### How to make change data capture (CDC) reliable in your data warehouse
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/change-data-capture
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data reliability
Summary: Replication looks solved until someone counts open orders in both places. Deletes that never arrive, duplicates after a restart, placeholder values overwriting real ones: the failure modes of change data capture are specific, and so are the fixes.

### Which dbt tests should you add first? A data quality starter set
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/is-our-data-reliable
Published: 2026-08-09; updated: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data reliability
Summary: Adding a test to every column feels thorough and ends in alert fatigue: hundreds of warnings nobody reads. Start with the tests that protect keys, joins, freshness and the totals the board sees, and give every one that can fail a run an owner.

### SCD type 2 in dbt: snapshots and point-in-time joins explained
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/customer-history-scd2
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: If your customer table is overwritten in place, every reassignment quietly restates history: last year's regional revenue changes and nobody signed it off. Keeping history is a modelling decision, and the joins that use it have sharp edges.

### How to upgrade to dbt v2 (Fusion) without breaking CI
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/dbt-fusion-upgrade
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: The dbt Fusion engine became generally available as dbt v2 in September 2026. Most upgrade breakages trace back to the deprecation warnings dbt 1.10 introduced, especially for teams running with --warn-error. Clear those first and the engine upgrade is mostly a rollout plan.

### How to speed up slow dbt runs: find the critical path first
URL: https://thebredge.com/insights/speed-up-dbt-runs
Published: 2026-10-21
Topic: Data systems
Summary: A dbt run that took twenty minutes now takes two hours, and the board numbers are late. The cause is rarely every model. Read run_results.json to find the slowest models and the chain that sets the finish time, then fix those.

## Public checklists and resources

### Reporting automation map and hours estimate
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/reporting-automation-map
Type: Calculator
Purpose: To automate a monthly report safely, map every step first and separate mechanical work from judgement. Mechanical steps move upstream into tested logic; judgement and the final review stay with people. This map estimates the hours that frees from your own inputs.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/automate-monthly-reporting

### Revenue reconciliation workbench
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/revenue-reconciliation-checklist
Type: Workbench
Purpose: To reconcile revenue between two systems, fix the definition and time range, match records on a shared key, then explain every difference by class until what is left is inside your tolerance. This workbench does the arithmetic and keeps the checklist with you.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/why-dashboards-disagree

### Hire vs fractional vs project: cost calculator
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/hire-vs-fractional-data-team-cost
Type: Calculator
Purpose: A data hire costs more than the salary: add employer on-costs, recruiting fees, tools, the months the seat is empty and the months it takes to ramp up. This calculator puts that next to a fractional team and a fixed project, using figures you enter, so you can see which is cheaper for your workload and when that flips.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/when-to-hire-a-data-team

### ARR bridge and cohort table builder
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/arr-bridge-cohort-builder
Type: Workbench
Purpose: An ARR bridge explains each month's change in recurring revenue as new, reactivated, expansion, contraction and churn; a cohort table shows how each month's new customers retain. Paste or upload one row per customer per month with their MRR, and the builder calculates both, plus trailing 12-month NRR and GRR, entirely in your browser.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/saas-metrics-from-stripe

### First data hire decision tree
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/first-data-hire-decision-tree
Type: Decision tree
Purpose: Your first data hire should match the constraint that blocks decisions today: an analyst if nobody has time to answer questions, an analytics engineer if the numbers disagree, a data engineer if data does not move reliably. Answer a few questions and the tree points to a role, a project or a fractional team.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/when-to-hire-a-data-team

### KPI dictionary template
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/kpi-dictionary-template
Type: Template
Purpose: A KPI dictionary is one agreed definition per metric: what it means, the formula, the grain, the source system, the owner and how currency is treated. Start from a pack below, edit it to your business, and export it to Excel or Google Sheets.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/why-dashboards-disagree

### Power BI refresh error lookup
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/power-bi-refresh-error-lookup
Type: Checklist
Purpose: Most Power BI refresh failures come from six causes: memory limits, the two- or five-hour timeout, an unreachable gateway, expired credentials, incremental refresh queries that do not fold, and a schedule switched off after four failures. Paste your error message and the lookup matches it to the documented cause, the fix steps and the Microsoft Learn page.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/power-bi-slow

### Power BI licensing cost calculator
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/power-bi-licensing-cost-calculator
Type: Calculator
Purpose: For most small teams, Pro for everyone is cheapest: $14 per user per month at Microsoft's US list price. Premium Per User at $24 makes sense when you need more than 8 refreshes a day or models over 1 GB. A Fabric F64 capacity pays off only when enough people view reports that their Pro licences cost more than the capacity, because on F64 and above viewers need only a free licence.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/power-bi-warehouse-or-both

### SaaS metrics definitions and calculator
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/saas-metrics-definitions
Type: Calculator
Purpose: SaaS metrics are only comparable when each one has a single written definition: what counts as recurring, which customers are in the cohort, and which costs are in acquisition. Enter one period's figures and the calculator returns MRR, ARR, NRR, GRR, churn and CAC payback with the formula shown for each.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/saas-metrics-from-stripe

### Data audit checklist and priority matrix
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/data-diagnostic-checklist
Type: Checklist
Purpose: A data audit inventories ten areas of your data setup, rates each one, then prioritises the problems by impact and effort. Rate your own setup here and the matrix sequences what to fix first, foundations before dashboards.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/is-our-data-reliable

### Data project brief template
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/data-project-brief-template
Type: Template
Purpose: A good data project brief states the decision the work serves, what is in and out of scope, the systems involved, how you will test that it is done, and who runs it afterwards. Fill in the sections here and copy a brief you can send to several suppliers, so their proposals answer the same question.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/when-to-hire-a-data-team

### Migration validation SQL generator
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/migration-validation-sql-generator
Type: Template
Purpose: Run the same checks on the old and the new system and compare the results: row counts by month, duplicate and missing keys, sums and ranges per column, and a fingerprint of every row by month. Describe the table once and the generator writes matching SQL for both dialects, with values formatted the same way on each engine so the results can be compared directly.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/change-data-capture

### Warehouse query cost estimator
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/warehouse-query-cost-estimator
Type: Calculator
Purpose: On BigQuery on-demand, cost is bytes scanned times your rate per TiB, and a dbt merge with a unique key is billed for the rows it reads plus the whole target table. On a large unpartitioned table, that makes an incremental merge dearer than a full rebuild. Enter your table size, row width, lookback and schedule to compare five build patterns per run and per month.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/incremental-models-at-scale

### dbt incremental strategy picker
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/dbt-incremental-strategy-picker
Type: Decision tree
Purpose: Use microbatch for append-only events on dbt 1.9 or later, merge for rows updated in place (delete+insert where merge fails on duplicate keys), a snapshot when you need past versions, and a plain table while a rebuild still takes minutes. Answer six questions and the picker returns the strategy for your adapter, a config block to copy, the edge cases to test and the commands to backfill history in ranges.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/incremental-models-at-scale

### dbt run_results.json analyser
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/dbt-run-results-analyser
Type: Workbench
Purpose: A slow dbt run is usually a handful of models and one long chain of dependencies, not the whole project. Upload run_results.json, and manifest.json if you have it, to see the slowest models, time by materialisation, how busy your threads were, the critical path that sets the minimum run time, and every failing test, all in your browser.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/incremental-models-at-scale

### Fivetran MAR cost estimator
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/fivetran-mar-cost-estimator
Type: Calculator
Purpose: Fivetran bills on monthly active rows: each distinct row inserted, updated or deleted in a month, counted per connection and table, once however often it changes. Enter the rows that change in each connection to estimate MAR, see what history mode adds, and cost it at your own effective rate.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/change-data-capture

### Backfill planner for billions of rows
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/backfill-planner
Type: Calculator
Purpose: Backfill billions of rows in date-range chunks that each finish well inside your job timeout, run a few at a time, oldest first, and make every chunk replace its own range so a rerun cannot duplicate data. Enter your history, a trial chunk's rows per second and your concurrency to get the chunk count, the running time, the commands and a progress table.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/incremental-models-at-scale

### Data freshness SLA calculator
URL: https://thebredge.com/resources/data-freshness-sla-calculator
Type: Calculator
Purpose: Worst-case staleness is the source lag plus, for every stage on its own schedule, its full interval and run time; a stage chained to the one before adds only its run time. Enter your connector, dbt and BI schedules to see the worst and typical staleness, whether your SLA holds, and the warn and error thresholds for dbt source freshness.
Related evidence and background: https://thebredge.com/insights/is-our-data-reliable

## Using and citing this index

- Read and cite the canonical page. Snippets here summarise the public source rather than replace it.
- Published dates describe the source metadata. No automated freshness or fabricated revisions are claimed.
- The synthetic data demonstrations on the homepage are illustrative, not customer testimonials or independently audited case studies. Review each original article for its own evidence and limitations.
- User-authorised browsers and agents may use the same public pages and contact form. There is no public machine-write credential, bot-trust bypass, or bulk-outreach permission.
- For actual enquiries use the browser form at https://thebredge.com/contact, subject to standard validation and rate limits.
- For booking use https://thebredge.com/schedule and obtain user approval of the selected time.
